title: AgentRunner seam: decouple agent runtime from Claude Code (C1)
description:
## What to build

Candidate 1 from the architecture review. Unite the Claude integration and the stub Gemini integration behind one deep AgentRunner interface so adding or swapping coding agents stops forking the whole stack. Two adapters already exist (Claude + Gemini) so the seam is real, not hypothetical.

Shape of the work:
1. Spike -> ADR defining the interface, plus proposed PRD EARS reqs + user story (multi-agent is currently PRD Out-of-Scope, line 166).
2. Route one narrow Claude path (branch-name completion) through the interface.
3. Prove the seam with a real Gemini adapter.
4. Migrate the remaining Claude paths (spawn, resume, parse) behind it.

Children: the spike + 5 implementation slices.

title: De-risk vendor coupling (architecture review program)
description:
## What to build

Program epic tracking the vendor-decoupling work from the architecture review (docs/architecture-review-vendor-decoupling.html). Goal: turn three vendor dependencies into swappable adapters at deep seams so the project outlives any one of them.

- C1 Anthropic / Claude Code  -> AgentRunner seam
- C2 frontend AgentMessage generalisation
- C3 GitHub / Codespaces      -> GitHost seam
- C4 W&B/CoreWeave-hosted catnip.run + Cloudflare -> HostedBackend adapter

Children: the C1 AgentRunner epic, the iOS baseURL win (a cheap C4 down-payment), and the signpost for C2-C4.

Note: local catnip run already survives a catnip.run shutdown (auth is gated on CATNIP_PROXY). This program is about designed optionality, not rescue.
notes: Source of truth: docs/architecture-review-vendor-decoupling.html. Top recommendation = C1 (only seam already justified by two live adapters).

title: Spike: design AgentRunner interface (ADR) to decouple workspace lifecycle from Claude Code
description:
## What to build

Design spike. Produce an ADR (docs/adr/0002-agentrunner-interface.md) defining a single deep AgentRunner interface that the existing Claude integration and the stub Gemini integration can both sit behind as adapters. The interface must cover what the workspace lifecycle needs from an agent: spawn an interactive session (PTY), resume/continue/fork a prior session, parse the agent streaming output into structured transcript events, expose session metadata (title, session id), and locate the agent per-project config/history dir.

Output is the ADR + proposed PRD changes — NOT implementation.

The PRD currently lists multi-agent support as Out of Scope (line 166) and gates the workspace lifecycle to the claude agent (R16/R17/R17a/R12). So the ADR shall also propose the new EARS requirements + user story that promote running non-Claude agents through the same workspace lifecycle into scope.

Source: architecture review docs/architecture-review-vendor-decoupling.html (candidate 1). Two adapters already exist (Claude + Gemini stub) so the seam is real, not hypothetical.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately
design: Deep AgentRunner seam unites ClaudeService + GeminiService (currently parallel copies). Interface is the test surface: one fake drives all callers.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] ADR written at docs/adr/0002-*.md following the docs/adr format
- [ ] AgentRunner interface defined: spawn, resume/continue/fork, parse-stream to events, session metadata, config-dir
- [ ] States how Claude and Gemini map onto the interface as adapters
- [ ] Records the deletion-test rationale (interface earns its keep across >=2 adapters)
- [ ] Proposes new EARS requirements + user story for PRD.md (generalising R12/R16/R17/R17a from Claude to agent)
- [ ] Human-approved; ready to /to-issues the implementation from the ADR
notes: Once the ADR is approved, run /to-issues against it to (re)generate implementation slices. The route-one-path / gemini-adapter / per-path-migration issues are the provisional C1 spine and may be refined by the ADR.

title: Add configurable backend baseURL to the iOS app
description:
## What to build

Cheap de-risk of the catnip.run hard dependency. The iOS app currently hardcodes the catnip.run backend URL. Add a configurable backend base URL (user setting or build config) so the app can point at a self-hosted Catnip backend instead of catnip.run. No behaviour change when left at the default.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately

PRD: R33, R34; supports US22 (self-host).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] iOS app reads backend baseURL from configuration, defaulting to catnip.run
- [ ] User can point the app at a self-hosted backend URL
- [ ] Auth and SSE clients honour the configured baseURL
- [ ] Builds via just build / just build-quick in xcode/

title: Migrate agent output stream parsing behind AgentRunner
description:
## What to build

Route the parse of the agent streaming output into structured transcript events (the parser deep module) through AgentRunner, including title extraction (R17). Each adapter owns its own output format; callers consume a common structured event shape.

## Blocked by

- Gemini AgentRunner adapter (catnap-jyf) — seam proven by two adapters

PRD: R17; parser deep module.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Output to structured-events parse exposed via AgentRunner
- [ ] Claude adapter parses its stream-json/jsonl format behind the interface
- [ ] Title extraction (R17) still works through the interface
- [ ] Common structured event shape consumed by callers (no Claude shape leaks)

title: Migrate session resume/continue/fork behind AgentRunner
description:
## What to build

Route session reattachment (resume/continue/fork of a prior session, R17a) through AgentRunner so resumption is expressed in interface terms, not Claude CLI flags.

## Blocked by

- Gemini AgentRunner adapter (catnap-jyf) — seam proven by two adapters

PRD: R17a.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Resume/continue/fork expressed via AgentRunner
- [ ] Claude adapter maps them onto its CLI semantics
- [ ] Resuming a prior session still reattaches correctly (R17a)
- [ ] Interface has no Claude-flag-specific surface

title: Migrate interactive session spawn (PTY) behind AgentRunner
description:
## What to build

Widen the seam: route interactive agent session spawning (starting the agent subprocess in a PTY for a workspace) through AgentRunner so the spawn path is agent-agnostic. Workspace terminals (R20) and concurrent per-workspace sessions (R16) go through the interface.

## Blocked by

- Gemini AgentRunner adapter (catnap-jyf) — seam proven by two adapters

PRD: R16, R20.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Interactive spawn goes through AgentRunner
- [ ] Claude adapter spawns via the interface; PTY/terminal behaviour unchanged
- [ ] Concurrent per-workspace sessions still keyed correctly (R16)
- [ ] Gemini adapter can spawn an interactive session through the same path

title: Add Gemini as a second AgentRunner adapter for completion
description:
## What to build

Prove the seam with a real second adapter. Implement a Gemini adapter for the same completion path established in the previous slice, so branch-name generation can run through Gemini as well as Claude. This is the first time a non-Claude agent actually runs a process (today Gemini only surfaces historical session summaries). Two live adapters validate the interface before wider migration.

## Blocked by

- Route Claude completion through AgentRunner (catnap-ewz)

PRD: promotes Out-of-Scope multi-agent (line 166) toward in-scope; R16/R17.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Gemini adapter implements AgentRunner for the completion path
- [ ] Agent selection picks Claude or Gemini for that path
- [ ] Both adapters pass the same interface-level tests
- [ ] No Claude-specific assumptions leak into the shared interface (deletion test holds)

title: Route Claude branch-name completion through AgentRunner
description:
## What to build

First tracer bullet through the new seam. Take one narrow existing Claude path — the completion call that turns a session title into a semantic branch name (R12) — and route it through the AgentRunner interface instead of calling the Claude integration directly. Claude becomes the first adapter. End-to-end: a titled session still produces a nice branch name, now via AgentRunner.

## Blocked by

- AgentRunner ADR spike (catnap-hv0)

PRD: R12; generalises agent orchestration R16/R17.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] AgentRunner interface exists in the backend per the approved ADR
- [ ] Claude adapter implements it for the completion path
- [ ] Branch-name generation (R12) calls the interface, not the concrete Claude integration
- [ ] Existing branch-name behaviour unchanged (verified by tests)
- [ ] A fake AgentRunner can drive the path in tests (interface is the test surface)

title: Signpost: vendor-decoupling candidates C2-C4 (AgentMessage, GitHost, HostedBackend)
description:
## What to build

Tracking/signpost issue for the deferred candidates from the architecture review (docs/architecture-review-vendor-decoupling.html). Not yet sliced for implementation — promote each via /to-issues (and, for the seams, a spike to ADR first) when its turn comes. Captured here so the work is not lost.

Deferred candidates:

- C2 generic AgentMessage type (frontend): introduce AgentMessage, convert transcript render; rename claude:message to agent:message and Worktree star-claude-star fields to agent-star end-to-end; namespace /v1/claude/star to /v1/agents/:agent/star. Depends on C1. PRD: R18, R23.
- C3 GitHost seam: spike to ADR defining a GitHost interface + first non-GitHub target (Forgejo/Codeberg), then a Forgejo PR-create adapter to prove it. Single host today so the seam stays hypothetical until a second adapter is on the table. PRD: promotes Out-of-Scope non-GitHub (line 167); R14/R15, R24, US24.
- C4 HostedBackend adapter: spike to ADR for an interface over sessions/codespace-creds/keepalive/assets, then a self-host adapter (Postgres + object storage) so Cloudflare/catnip.run become swappable. PRD: R28-R32, US22, US9.

## Blocked by

None - tracking only
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Revisited after C1 lands; each candidate promoted via spike to ADR to /to-issues when prioritised
